chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Zur'ah from Samaanah and Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abi Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man is obligated to pay zakat, and he has needy relatives who are not aware (of the obligation or the payment); should he give them the zakat? He said: 'No, and for the sake of honor, he should not make the zakat a shield to protect his wealth; he should give them from other than the zakat if he wishes.'
As for the one to whom zakat is not permissible, it has been narrated (about him).
ai.seo_question: Can a man give zakat to his relatives if they are unaware of the payment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that zakat is not a tool for self-aggrandizement; if a man gives zakat to relatives who are unaware, it serves merely as a shield to protect his own wealth from being spent on them. To truly honor them, he must give from his voluntary wealth (sadaqah) rather than the obligatory zakat, ensuring the charity is for their benefit and not his own financial preservation. This ruling highlights the distinction between the legal obligation of zakat and the spiritual virtue of maintaining kinship ties through personal generosity.
